items.title: Musk Won’t Take Stock Awards “Simply for Merging With SpaceX.” Tesla Shareholders Still Have to Vote
items.summary: Key TakeawaysElon Musk said at the DealBook Summit that he shouldn’t receive Tesla stock awards just for merging Tesla with SpaceX. That eases a real dilution worry, since his 2025 pay package covers 423.

items.title: Trump Calls Huang’s Exit “Such a Tragedy” as His Filing Shows Up to $380,000 of Nvidia Buys
items.summary: Key TakeawaysTrump’s September trading report shows up to $380,000 of Nvidia buys, plus Tesla and SpaceX, and sales of $1 million to $5 million each of Home Depot and McDonald’s. The White House says outside firms run the portfolio, and most of the month’s money went into a dividend ETF and municipal bonds.

items.title: H-E-B, Southwest, Dell lead Forbes' best Texas companies list
items.summary: H-E-B beat out Southwest, Dell and ExxonMobil to top Forbes’ new list of the best companies based in Texas. Tesla squeaked in at No. 25.

items.title: Elon Musk Calls Anthropic’s Models ‘Great Products,’ Jassy Says ‘We’re Big Believers’: Mag 7 Voices This Week
items.summary: Elon Musk called Anthropic’s Opus and Fable models “great products” and described the company’s leadership as “principled” and “diligent.”

items.title: The Danger of Jensen Huang’s Handshake Deals at Nvidia
items.summary: The ousted CEO once celebrated his no-contract deals but now they look like red flags.

items.title: MKBHD Says He Will Honor Tesla Cybercab’s 2024 Bet, Elon Musk Says ‘Fair Enough’: ‘I Will Accept Delivery…’
items.summary: Marques Brownlee confirmed he has placed an order for the vehicle, prompting CEO Elon Musk to respond briefly but approvingly on social media.

items.title: In 2000, Elon Musk Crashed His Uninsured $1 Million McLaren Trying to Show Peter Thiel What It Could Do. In 2025, Thiel’s Fund Quietly Sold Every Tesla Share It Owned
items.summary: In 2000 Musk crashed his uninsured $1 million McLaren F1 with Peter Thiel aboard. In 2025 Thiel's hedge fund sold all 272,613 of its Tesla shares, the last in the quarter the stock hit its record, and its filing on Monday shows it still owns none.

items.title: Has AI's honeymoon ended on Wall Street?
items.summary: Although the AI industry has been the darling of Wall Street for years, the sector now makes investors wince as it reckons with a wave of concerns over dizzying spending and its promise to make the technology profitable.But as spending has ballooned, so has debt -- and profits have yet to match.
